sections.h2: Where does Carol Stream sit in DuPage County?
sections.html:
Carol Stream is a village in DuPage County, Illinois, in the western Chicago suburbs. It was incorporated on January 5, 1959, and 39,854 people lived there at the 2020 census.

The village covers 9.44 square miles, of which 9.12 are land and 0.32 are water. That is a compact footprint for nearly 40,000 people. The village dates only from 1959, so the housing stock is young by Chicago-area standards.

  • County: DuPage, with deeds recorded at the DuPage County Recorder
  • Village government: a mayor and six trustees, with an appointed village administrator
  • Parks: 36 parks run by the Carol Stream Park District

sections.h2: How did Carol Stream get started?
sections.html:
Developer Jay Stream began buying unincorporated farmland outside Wheaton in 1957, after a frustrating run-in with red tape on a Naperville subdivision, and named the new community for his daughter Carol.

The first village board meeting took place on February 12, 1959. The population was 836 in the 1960 census, then climbed to 4,434 in 1970, 15,472 in 1980 and 31,716 in 1990. It peaked near 40,438 in 2000, slipped to 39,711 in 2010 and stood at 39,854 in 2020.

A former Gretna railway station was renamed Carol Stream in 1962 and now serves as a museum for the Carol Stream Historical Society. The pattern of fast growth followed by a flat decade is useful to a seller: most neighbors bought within the same few decades, so comparable sales tend to be houses of similar age.

sections.h2: Which employers shape the Carol Stream housing market?
sections.html:
Carol Stream's jobs lean toward warehousing, food production and printing rather than one anchor company. The village's 2022 annual financial report, as summarized in the encyclopedia entry for the village, lists these largest employers:

  • Hearthside Food Solutions, 650 employees
  • FIC America Corp., 494
  • Grunt Style, 400
  • FedEx, 369
  • American Litho, 350
  • Tyndale House Publishers, 260

The United States Postal Service also runs a sectional hub here for ZIP codes beginning 601 and 603. Because the employer base is spread across several industries, a layoff at one plant is unlikely to empty the neighborhood, though it can affect a seller who has to move on a short timeline.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve homes in Carol Stream?
sections.html:
Carol Stream's village limits do not match school district lines, so the district depends on the street address. Buyers ask about this early, and a seller who can answer it removes one question from the showing.

  • Most homes: Community Consolidated School District 93 for kindergarten through eighth grade, then Glenbard Township High School District 87 and Glenbard North High School
  • Northwest corner: Elgin Area School District U46, with Spring Trail Elementary in the village
  • Part of the west side: Benjamin School District 25, then Community High School District 94 and West Chicago Community High School
  • Some southern and southeastern blocks: Community Unit School District 200 in Wheaton, or Glen Ellyn School District 41 with Glenbard North for high school

District 93 runs eight schools in the village, including Jay Stream Middle School, named for the founder, and Stratford Middle School.

sections.h2: What roads and transit connect Carol Stream?
sections.html:
North Avenue runs east and west near the middle of the village and is the main corridor, with Army Trail Road and Geneva Road as the other major east-west routes. Gary Avenue runs north and south toward Bloomingdale and the Stratford Square area, and County Farm Road is a major commercial route. Schmale Road serves a small commercial pocket in the southeast, and Kuhn Road runs north and south as a lesser route.

Pace operates Route 711 between Carol Stream and Wheaton. The Great Western Trail crosses town, and the Steve Ravanesi Trail links it to Red Hawk Park, the dog park and Glenbard North High School. A house within a short walk of the trail or a park district facility has an easy item to put in a listing description.

sections.h2: What does Carol Stream require before a sale can close?
sections.html:
The village charges its own transfer tax, and the stamp has to be obtained before closing paperwork goes to the recorder. The rate printed on the Finance Department page is $3.00 for each $1,000 of the selling price or fraction thereof.

Carol Stream transfer stamp checklist, from the Village of Carol Stream Finance Department page
ItemWhat the village page says
Where stamps are issuedFinance Department at the village's main offices
FormsSigned transfer stamp declaration and the State of Illinois transfer declaration
ContractCopy of the fully executed contract showing the price
WaterFinal meter reading booked at least 2 working days before closing; final bill paid before the stamp is issued
Exempt deeds$25 administrative fee for exempt stamps

Contracts can be emailed to the Finance Department, with a 25MB file limit and no zip files. Call the Water Billing division at 630-871-6222 to set the meter reading. Most readings are taken by radio, so the village does not usually need to enter the house.

sections.h2: Who pays the village tax, and can it be refunded?
sections.html:
The seller, or grantor, normally owes the village tax. When a property passes through a sheriff's sale or a tax deed, the buyer owes it instead.

The village allows a refund only when every one of four conditions is met. The seller must have lived in the house for a year within the last three, must not have rented out any part of it, must have bought and now occupy a replacement home inside the village, and must apply within one year of paying the tax. A seller who moves out of Carol Stream will not qualify for this refund.

sections.h2: Do permits matter when I sell a Carol Stream house?
sections.html:
Yes, since an unclosed permit is a question a buyer's agent or the closing attorney may raise. Permit applications go through the Community Development Department, either online or in person, and the village notes a card fee of 2.9 percent online and 3.5 percent at the counter.

  • Inspections need about 24 hours of advance notice and are scheduled at 630-871-6230 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.
  • Plumbing inspections are done by a consultant on Monday, Wednesday and Friday afternoons, 1:30 to 3:30 p.m.
  • A re-inspection fee can apply if work fails or is not ready, and it must be paid before the next visit

If you remember a finished basement, deck or water heater swap from a previous owner, ask Community Development whether the permit was closed out. A cash buyer purchasing as-is absorbs that question, while a retail buyer's lender may want it settled.

sections.h2: What state and county steps apply to a sale here?
sections.html:
The state adds its own levy on title transfers under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, at half a dollar for each $500 of declared value. The declaration is filed through the state's MyDec system, and the Carol Stream stamp requires a copy of it.

Your deed is filed with the DuPage County Recorder, whose land records reach back to 1839. The recorder's office can be reached at 630-407-5400, and it also provides deed copies if you need one for a tax appeal or an exemption.

sections.h2: How do listing, selling yourself and a cash offer compare in Carol Stream?
sections.html:
Listing with an agent puts the house in front of the widest group of buyers, which suits a house in good shape and an owner who can wait through showings, inspection requests and a buyer's mortgage approval. Selling it yourself saves the agent's fee but leaves the contract, disclosures and the village stamp paperwork on your desk.

An as-is cash sale fits a house that needs work, has a tenant in it, came through an estate or faces a tight deadline. The trade-off is that a cash offer is usually below what a fully repaired house might bring on the open market. Weigh the offer against the repair bill, the carrying costs while the house sits, and the time you have.

faqs.q: Do I pay the Carol Stream transfer tax as the seller?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The village page says the tax generally falls on the grantor, the seller, with an exception for sheriff's sales and tax deeds, where the buyer pays. The rate shown is $3.00 per $1,000 of the price or fraction thereof.

faqs.q: How soon before closing should I book the water meter reading?
faqs.a: Book it at least two working days before closing. Call the Water Billing division at 630-871-6222. The final bill, and anything else owed to the village, must be paid before the stamp is issued.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Carol Stream house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Most homes are in District 93 and Glenbard North, while parts of the village fall in U46, District 25, District 200 or District 41. Check the boundary with the district before you advertise the house.

faqs.q: Can I sell if a past owner skipped a permit?
faqs.a: Yes, you can still sell, but the issue may come up in an inspection or title review. Ask the Community Development Department at 630-871-6230 about the permit history. An as-is cash buyer may take the risk on, while a financed buyer may ask you to resolve it first.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded after the sale?
faqs.a: With the DuPage County Recorder, the county's land records office. The state transfer declaration and the village stamp are completed before recording. Call 630-407-5400 with questions about recording.
